claims.notes: [BATCH NOTE b074 RE-EXTRACT 2] Second re-extraction of this range, under charter § 5 rule 14. Supersedes the previous 074.json, which was cut against a 652-line body; the document is 663 lines at HEAD and this file covers lines 333-663 only (sibling batch b073 covers 1-332, unchanged). WHAT MOVED: the 2026-08-04 changelog entry's closing clause was found FALSE by a blind verification pass and withdrawn in place — the sentence at lines 573-576 now stops at 'holds **4,746** features at this commit.' and a blockquoted correction occupies new lines 578-590, so every claim that previously sat below line 577 has shifted by +11. Every line number in this file was re-verified against HEAD rather than arithmetically shifted on trust. THE WITHDRAWN SENTENCE: 'and the D-S aggregations documented here consume the separate legacy layer `inputs/vectors/references/student-mounds-55maps.geojson` (see § 6), not the reviewed layer at all' is quoted at lines 579-581 as text the document NO LONGER ASSERTS, so it is not extracted as a live claim; it carries no numeral in any case (its only figure-like token, '§ 6', is a section reference out of scope under rule 5), so it yields no claim row at all — had it carried a number, that number would have been method 'historical' per rule 3. THE OPEN D-S FINDING: the two figures the correction reports — a 4,745-point student ground truth implied by the image run's Dawid–Skene fit, and a 4,770-feature legacy layer implied by the other three — are extracted at lines 584-586 as an OPEN, UNADJUDICATED finding, all values method 'anchor-unknown' with a null anchor, because the document explicitly escalates rather than asserts which layer each fit consumed; chase targets are named in that claim's notes. LEGACY vs REVIEWED LAYER: § 6 (line 415) names inputs/vectors/references/student-mounds-55maps.geojson as the D-S student GT, and the correction now flags that whether all four fits consumed it is unverified. That layer is NOT the reviewed layer inputs/vectors/references/student-mounds-55maps-reviewed.geojson whose live count (4,746) is read at lines 562-567 and 573-576 — the two must not be conflated, and the one claim in this range that puts a number on the legacy layer (4,770, line 586) is anchor-unknown for the reason above. LIVE-vs-HISTORICAL split in the changelog: in every before→after table and every 'was X, now Y' sentence the Before / 'was' side is method 'historical' with a null path, and the After / artefact-value side is a live 'read' (or 'arithmetic' where the cell is derived), per instrument rule 3. The three 2026-08-04 rows (§§ 4.1, 4.3, 5.4) therefore each carry 0.8332 as historical and 0.8333 as a live read of results/55maps-image-generalisation/corrected-f1-multi-buffer/summary.json; the five 2026-08-03 rows follow the same pattern against the ds-human-crosstab / dawid-skene artefacts the entry itself names. GROUND-TRUTH COUNTS: every 4,745 (and the single 4,744) in this range describes what a past evaluation consumed or what a past fit implies, not the current canonical count, and none is anchored to the live GeoJSON — the canonical timeline recorded at reports/verification/c4-triage/coverage-drift-2026-08-04.json#$.gt_count_era_resolution shows the 2026-05-03 evaluations ran between baf1497a7 (4,744→4,745) and 2e075eb99 (4,745→4,746), so anchoring them to the live reviewed GeoJSON would manufacture a false mismatch. Era artefacts still carrying 4,745 at $.results[0].n_ref_student_only, if triage wants a live check: results/55maps-image-generalisation/corrected-f1-multi-buffer/summary.json.pre-dedup-rerun-20260804T000000.backup, plus the un-regenerated T=0.7 and text-MIN corrected-f1-multi-buffer summaries. Only the two 4,746 assertions (lines 566-567 and 576) and the artefact restatement at line 542 are live reads. SCOPE DECISIONS for this batch (instrument rule 5): dates, timestamps, git hashes, session numbers, Obs / erratum / escalation identifiers (Obs 268/269/273/293, W6-E9, W7-E4, D17, FALSE-12, P4, R4), version strings (v1, v2, GS-v2), § section references (§ 3, § 4.1, § 4.3, § 5.2, § 5.4, § 6, § 6.1), candidate and map-sheet identifiers (cand 2397, K-35-064-3), decimal-place descriptors ('4 d.p.', '3 d.p.', 'third-decimal', 'fourth-decimal'), and numbers inside paths or condition names (T=0.3, T=0.7, consensus-4of5, .../bounds/384/..., the wave7-w7e4 blind-pass filename) are all excluded. Bibliographic metadata in § 7 (Dawid & Skene 1979, 28(1), 20-28; Sobotkova et al. 2023) is citation apparatus, not a claim about the study, so the only § 7 claim extracted is the Obs 293 gloss at lines 514-516, which asserts run counts. Buffer radii written purely to identify which row a metric belongs to ('at R = 50 m', 'R = 50 m' in a changelog cell label) are treated as locators, not claims; the one place the document asserts R_m as artefact content (line 542) IS extracted. Run-count words ('the four runs', 'the other three runs') are extracted where they occur in flowing prose and left as anchor-unknown, but not where they appear inside a table cell label or a section heading. CLAIM-SPECIFIC: prose restatement of the § 4.2 ratio column. The T=0.7 figure here reads 1.92× — the 2026-08-03 wave-6 repair moved it from 1.90×, and the changelog entry at lines 636-640 records that transition; both spans are extracted separately.
